newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two Sri Lankan rebel officials shot dead in Paris.
newsitem.headline: Two Sri Lankan rebel officials shot dead in Paris.

text.p: Rebel Sri Lankan Tamils said on Sunday two of the group's officials were shot dead in Paris and blamed the killings on Tamils collaborating with the Colombo government.

A statement from the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) received in Paris named the victims as their treasurer Kandiah Perinpanathan, and Kandiah Gajendran, editor of the Tamil weekly newspaper Eela Murasu.
A Paris police spokesman said two Sri Lankan Tamils, both in their 30s, were shot dead in the heavily-immigrant La Chapelle district of northern Paris overnight by a gunman who escaped.
An Interior Ministry spokesman confirmed one of the victims was Perinpanathan but named the other as Kandiah Gajan. There was no immediate explanation for the discrepancy on the name.

The Tamil Tiger rebels are fighting the Colombo government for an independent Tamil homeland in the Indian Ocean island's north and east. More than 50,000 people have died in the ethnic war, now in its 14th year, according to government figures.

"The LTTE condemns the killing of Mr Kandiah Perinpanathan, head of the finance section of the LTTE International Secretariat, and the editor of the Tamil weekly newspaper Eela Murasu Mr Kandiah Gajendran," said the statement issued by the London-based LTTE International Secretariat.
It said the killings were part of the Sri Lankan government's attempt to hit the rebels' finances, and appeared to blame Tamils cooperating with Colombo.
It said Tamils should be aware that "elements within the Tamil society actively participate with the Sri Lanka government's genocidal war on the Tamil people inside and outside".

"This dastardly act is considered by our organisation as part of the Sri Lankan government's international conspiracy to destroy the legitimate struggle of the Tamil people for freedom and peace by curbing the financial assistance provided by Tamil people all over the world," it added.
Colombo has said it believes Tamil rebels finance their military activity through funds extorted from expatriate Sri Lankans in Western countries.

Sri Lanka's Justice and Constitutional Affairs Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris said during a visit to Washington earlier this month that the United States was expected to include the LTTE on a list of terrorist groups being drawn up for completion probably by the end of this year.
Peiris said this would mean that the group's bank assets in the United States would be frozen and its members deported and barred from entering the country.

Many western nations have condemned the LTTE for the bombing of Sri Lanka's central bank in January which killed nearly 100 people, and for the July bombing of a packed train in a suburb of Colombo in which 57 died.
